newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 22.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Thursday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Toyota Motor Corp and Honda Motor Co Ltd plan to limit car exports to the United States in fiscal 1997/98 to previous year's level.
-- Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto decides against including Uruguay Round farm appropriations in supplementary budget.
-- U.S. trade deficit with Japan rises 8.3 percent in March.
-- Toyota Motor Corp reports 82 percent increase in pre-tax profit.
-- Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd executives to step down over corporate racketeer scandal.
-- Japan-U.S. defence review to cover repairs and medical treatment for U.S. soldiers.
-- Health and Welfare Ministry to tighten incinerator regulations to curb dioxin.
-- Posts & Telecommunications Ministry to freeze postage prices until 2005.
-- Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank aware of racketeer's plans to use loans to buy massive shares in brokerages.
-- Lower House panel to approve bills on care of elderly on Thursday.
